skill.name: ai-avatar-video
skill.description: Create AI avatar, talking head, and lip sync video workflows with the inference.sh belt CLI. It focuses on P-Video-Avatar, OmniHuman, Fabric, PixVerse, text to speech, dubbing, and UGC-style production.
skill.summary: Create avatar and talking head videos with inference.sh belt workflows.
skill.author: halt-catch-fire

security_audit.summary: No prompt injection attempt was found in SKILL.md. The skill intentionally relies on the belt CLI and external inference services, so confirmed risks center on command execution, third-party media processing, and synthetic presenter misuse.

remediation.suggestion: Limit allowed-tools to the smallest required belt commands and require confirmation for app-store or install actions.
Add clear privacy guidance that portraits, scripts, audio, and video URLs are sent to inference.sh or model providers.
Move npx skill-install examples behind manual review and pin trusted sources or versions where possible.
Add consent, rights, and disclosure checks before creating avatar, UGC, or endorsement content.
Use a marketplace-hosted asset or remove remote images if tracking or availability is a concern.

content.value_statement: Creating avatar videos often requires model selection, voice setup, and multi-step media workflows. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through inference.sh avatar video commands and safe input planning.
actual_capabilities: Runs inference.sh belt commands for P-Video-Avatar examples.
Creates talking head videos from portrait URLs and written scripts.
Uses audio URLs for lip sync models such as OmniHuman, Fabric, and PixVerse.
Shows workflows for portrait generation, text to speech, dubbing, and avatar video.
Compares avatar model cost, speed, and built-in TTS support.
Provides batch examples for multiple presenters and voices.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh belt CLI, an account, and network access.
Media URLs, scripts, and audio may be sent to third-party inference services.
It does not verify consent, identity rights, or disclosure requirements.
Output quality depends on source media, voice choice, and model availability.

use_cases.title: Create product presenter videos
use_cases.description: Marketing teams can turn approved portraits and scripts into short product videos with virtual presenters.

use_cases.title: Produce lesson introductions
use_cases.description: Educators can create talking head introductions for course modules using selected voices and languages.

use_cases.title: Localize existing videos
use_cases.description: Localization teams can transcribe, translate, generate speech, and lip sync videos for new audiences.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic avatar clip
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with one portrait and one script.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 30-second avatar video from this portrait URL and script. Use P-Video-Avatar with built-in TTS and a friendly English voice.

prompt_templates.title: Choose the best model
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare P-Video-Avatar, OmniHuman, Fabric, and PixVerse for a one-minute product explainer. Recommend the best model and explain cost, speed, and audio needs.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a full production workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow with image generation and speech design.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a workflow to generate a portrait, create expressive speech, and produce a vertical avatar video for a product launch. Include inputs I must prepare.

prompt_templates.title: Design a batch campaign
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced batch request with governance checks.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a batch process for three presenters and two languages using approved portraits and scripts. Include consent checks and where each output is used.

output_examples.input: A marketing manager asks for a product demo from one approved portrait and a 45-second script.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends P-Video-Avatar, lists required portrait and script inputs, selects a voice, and warns that media is sent to inference.sh.

output_examples.input: A course creator needs the same lesson intro in English and Spanish.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests built-in TTS when possible, or a separate speech step, then a lip sync step for each language.

output_examples.input: A social team wants three short UGC-style clips with different presenters.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines a batch workflow with separate voices, approved images, consistent resolution, and clear labeling as synthetic media.

best_practices: Use only portraits and voices where you have consent and usage rights.
Review generated videos for accuracy, disclosure, and brand safety before publishing.
Use clear media URLs and keep private assets out of public links when possible.
anti_patterns: Do not create videos that impersonate real people without authorization.
Do not send confidential customer media to external services without approval.
Do not install related skills or CLIs from unreviewed sources during a production task.

faq.question: Does this skill create videos locally?
faq.answer: No. It uses the inference.sh belt CLI and external models, so network access is required.

faq.question: Which model does it recommend first?
faq.answer: It recommends P-Video-Avatar because the source says it is faster, cheaper, and includes text to speech.

faq.question: Can it use my own audio?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples show audio URL inputs for lip sync and avatar models.

faq.question: Can it generate portraits too?
faq.answer: Yes. The source includes a workflow using P-Image before creating the avatar video.

faq.question: What should I prepare before using it?
faq.answer: Prepare an approved portrait, a short script, voice preferences, output resolution, and any required disclosure text.

faq.question: Is consent handled automatically?
faq.answer: No. You must verify rights, consent, and disclosure requirements before generating or publishing avatar videos.
